check_service_status.description: See whether VIES is up and which countries' VAT systems are answering right now. Countries go offline for maintenance regularly, and a number from one of them cannot be checked while it is - so a nightly run can look here first and wait rather than fill a customer list with rows it could not check. This is the one step that reports trouble as a value instead of failing, so a workflow can branch on it. No account or API key required.

check_vat_format.description: Check whether a VAT number has the shape its country publishes - nine digits for Germany, U and eight for Austria - without contacting VIES at all. Instant, and free of the rate limits a real check runs into, so it is the right thing to put behind a signup form or in front of a long list. It is a guide, not a verdict: only Validate a VAT number can say whether a number is actually registered. No account or API key required.

simulate_validation.description: Ask VIES's own test service for a chosen outcome - registered, not registered, the country's system down, VIES too busy - and see exactly what your workflow would get, including the message it would show. Nothing real is checked, and unlike every other step here this one hands a failure back as data instead of stopping. No account or API key required.

validate_vat_number.description: Check an EU VAT number against the official register of the country that issued it, and get back whether it is registered, along with the business's name and address where that country publishes them. This is the check that lets you zero-rate a cross-border sale, so it never guesses: if VIES or the country cannot be reached, the step stops and says so rather than reporting the number as invalid. Paste the number as it is written on the invoice - IE6388047V, spaces and all. No account or API key required.

validate_vat_numbers.description: Check a whole list of VAT numbers in one step - a customer export, a signup batch, a quarterly re-check of everyone you invoice - and get one row per number saying valid, not registered, or not checked. A country going quiet halfway through costs that one row and not the run, and a row that could not be checked says so plainly rather than being counted as invalid. Up to 50 numbers at a time, checked at a pace VIES is happy to serve. No account or API key required.

description: Confirm that an EU VAT number is genuinely registered, straight from the European Commission's VIES service - the official source, which passes every check live to the tax administration of the country that issued the number. Validate one number or a whole customer list, get the registered business name and address back where the country publishes them, compare a company's name and address with the register, and check the number's format offline before you ever contact VIES. Add your own VAT number once and every check comes back with the consultation number tax authorities accept as proof you verified a customer. A check that could not be made is never reported as an invalid number. No account or API key required.
